title: What to Wear to a Casual Wedding
metaTitle: What to Wear to a Casual Wedding: For Women and Men
metaDescription: What to wear to a casual wedding: Emily Post's lists for women and men, a jeans verdict, venue-by-venue advice, and why white is the top guest worry.
h1: What to Wear to a Casual Wedding, for Women and Men
answer: For a casual wedding, women wear a sundress, an easy midi dress, or a skirt or dressy trousers with a nice top. Men wear khakis or slacks with a button-down or a polo, a sport coat optional, and loafers. Casual still means dressed for an event: skip athleisure, flip-flops, graphic tees and anything white. Wear jeans only if the couple or the venue clearly invites them.
intro: Knowing what to wear to a casual wedding comes down to one gap: the distance between everyday casual and casual for a wedding. The Emily Post Institute publishes both versions, and they disagree on jeans, shorts, T-shirts and whether men need a jacket. This guide puts the two lists side by side for women and men, rules on the pieces guests hesitate over, adjusts for backyard, barn, beach, park and restaurant venues, and shows what 250 casual-wedding outfit posts on Reddit actually asked. White came first, by a wide margin.

contentSections.heading: Emily Post's casual list vs. its informal wedding columns
contentSections.content:
The Emily Post Institute publishes two lists that answer this question, and they do not say quite the same thing. The first is its general casual list, written for any casual event, where the standard is clothing that is "informal and comfortable, yet clean and professional." The second is its wedding guest chart, whose least formal column is "informal." Read side by side, they show how far a wedding pulls casual upward.

Casual, any event (Emily Post Attire Guide):
• Women: a sundress; a long or short skirt; khakis or nice jeans; shorts, depending on occasion and climate; a plain T-shirt with no slogans, a polo or a turtleneck; a casual button-down blouse.
• Men: khakis or good jeans (clean, no holes); cargo or Bermuda shorts, depending on occasion and climate; a plain T-shirt, polo or turtleneck; a casual button-down and/or a sweater; loafers, sneakers or sandals.

Informal wedding (Emily Post Wedding Guest Attire):
• Daytime, women: an afternoon dress, or a dressy skirt or pants with a blouse.
• Daytime, men: a sports jacket or blazer with slacks, tie optional.
• Evening, women: an afternoon or cocktail dress.
• Evening, men: a blazer with grey flannels or slacks, tie optional.

What drops out between the two lists is the useful part. Jeans, shorts, T-shirts and sneakers sit on the everyday list and nowhere on the wedding one. What gets added is a jacket for men, day and night, and after dark, a dress for women that could pass at a cocktail party. The institute's note on its own casual list points the same way: "go with nicer casual wear and avoid the baggier items you wear around the house."

So the working rule is simple. Treat "casual" on a wedding invitation as the dressy end of the everyday list, and treat the informal wedding column as the ceiling you can reach without overdressing. Anything in the overlap is safe: a sundress, or a skirt and blouse, for women; slacks and a button-down, with a jacket in hand, for men.

contentSections.heading: Can you wear jeans to a casual wedding?
contentSections.content:
Usually not, unless the couple or the setting invites them. Emily Post's everyday casual list includes nice jeans for women and good, clean jeans for men, but its informal wedding columns leave denim out and list dresses, skirts, pants and slacks instead. Vogue's guide reaches the same ruling in plainer words: steer clear of flip-flops, graphic tees and blue denim "unless it fits the venue," and she gives denim at a ranch wedding as her example of dressing for the surroundings.

That leaves three cases:
• The invitation or wedding website mentions jeans, denim, boots or a western theme. Dark, clean jeans are fine. Dress the top half up: a blouse or dressy top for women, a button-down and a sport coat for men.
• The venue is a ranch or a working barn and nothing else is said. Jeans are defensible, but chinos or a midi dress are still the safer call.
• Anywhere else, including backyards, parks and restaurants. Skip denim, and that includes a denim jacket thrown over a dress.

The table below runs the same test on the other pieces guests hesitate over. Each verdict comes from the two Emily Post lists and Goldberg's advice in Vogue; where those sources say nothing about an item, the note names the rule that decides it.

contentSections.heading: For men, aim for the top of the casual list
contentSections.content:
Men's casual has a wider range than women's, so the real question is which end of it to aim for. Emily Post's everyday list runs all the way down to cargo shorts, a plain T-shirt and sneakers. Its informal wedding columns start at a sports jacket or blazer with slacks, tie optional, by day, and a blazer with grey flannels or slacks, tie optional, in the evening. Goldberg's view in Vogue sits slightly below that: a button-down and slacks are a safe choice, a polo works if it isn't sporty golf-shirt fabric, casual "does not require a jacket and tie," and a sports jacket "won't have you feeling out of place."

Put together, a practical outfit is:
• Trousers: chinos or slacks. Tailored shorts only at a hot daytime summer wedding where the couple's tone is plainly relaxed (Vogue allows them for summer).
• Shirt: a crisp button-down, or a knit polo in a fine fabric. Vogue also suggests a crisp white T-shirt under a suit as a way to make the suit read casual.
• Jacket: optional by day, but bring one for an evening reception or an indoor venue, since that is what Emily Post's informal evening column lists.
• Tie: optional in every source.
• Shoes: loafers, boat shoes, or clean all-leather sneakers rather than athletic ones (Goldberg).

The jacket is the piece that solves an ambiguous invitation. With it on, you are dressed for the top of casual and the bottom of dressy casual, which covers both readings of the word. Without it, you are still correct by Vogue's standard. A suit in a light color or a soft fabric, worn without a tie, also works and is easier than buying separates if a suit is what you own.

contentSections.heading: Match the venue and the season, for women and men
contentSections.content:
Goldberg's advice is to let the venue set the mood: casual "is your invitation to lean into your surroundings." Here is what to wear to a casual wedding at each of the settings these weddings most often use. None of it overrides the invitation; if the couple names a code or a theme, follow that first.

• Backyard. Goldberg's example for women is a floral-printed midi. Men: chinos with a button-down or fine-knit polo, jacket optional by day. Both: shoes that cope with grass, such as block heels or flat sandals, and loafers or leather sneakers rather than thin dress soles.
• Barn or ranch. The one setting where denim can belong (see the jeans rules above). Women: a midi dress or skirt, with boots if the theme invites them. Men: chinos or, where invited, dark jeans, a button-down, and a sport coat for the evening part.
• Beach. Vogue says beach weddings can call for more sandals and resort-wear looks, and Goldberg's beach-club example is a breezy caftan. Men: light trousers, a linen-look or cotton shirt, and leather sandals or loafers; the men's beach attire guide covers fabrics and sand in detail. A flat leather sandal does the job a flip-flop would, and reads as deliberate.
• Park or garden. Vogue notes that a garden setting suggests floral prints and light pastel colors. Men can follow the same lighter palette in chinos and shirting. Public parks often mean uneven ground and long walks from parking, so plan shoes accordingly.
• Restaurant or brewery. Indoors and usually in the evening, so dress to Emily Post's informal evening column: an afternoon or cocktail dress for women, a blazer with slacks for men.

Season works on both outfits at once. Emily Post qualifies shorts on its casual list with "depending on occasion and climate," and Vogue allows tailored shorts at a summer wedding, so heat is the main reason to pare down. For cool-weather casual weddings, swap to heavier fabrics, longer sleeves and closed-toe shoes; men can add a sweater, which is on Emily Post's casual list, or move up to the blazer. Vogue's time-of-day test helps in every season: dress for a daytime wedding as you would for a nice lunch, and for an evening one as you would for dinner.

contentSections.heading: White comes first: what casual guests actually ask
contentSections.content:
In our analysis of 10,700 posts on r/Weddingattireapproval (16 April – 21 October 2026), 250 carried the Casual dress-code flair. We counted how many of those 250 mention each topic in their title or text, using fixed keyword lists. 82 mention white, ivory, cream or champagne, about a third, and that is more than any other topic counted. Venue words such as outdoor, garden, beach, barn, backyard or park appear in 52, shoes in 36, black in 18, and jeans or denim in 15. Worry about being overdressed (15 posts) was as common as worry about being underdressed (13).

The white count makes sense once you picture the clothes. Casual weddings are mostly daytime and warm-weather, and the obvious outfit for that is a light summer dress, so the line between "pale" and "bridal" is exactly where casual guests get stuck. Etiquette expert Elaine Swann, speaking to TODAY, puts it plainly: "Any shades of white, that color is still reserved for the bride," unless the couple asks guests to wear it. The practical test: if the dress could be mistaken for white in a photo, especially in direct sun, choose another. A print with a light ground counts as white if the white dominates.

The same rule applies to men in a softer form. A white shirt is standard; a head-to-toe white or cream suit at a daytime wedding draws the same attention a white dress does, so keep at least the trousers or jacket in another color.

Black came up far less often. It is generally fine at a casual wedding, though at a bright daytime event it can read heavier than the setting; the guide to wearing black to a wedding covers it in full.

contentSections.heading: When to dress up a notch
contentSections.content:
Emily Post's guidance is that "the wedding invitation and the time of the wedding will be your best guide to its formality," and Vogue closes on the same instinct: "when in doubt, choose the slightly more tailored ensemble." These are the situations where that applies:

• It starts after dark. The informal evening column moves women to an afternoon or cocktail dress and keeps men in a blazer.
• It is indoors, at a restaurant, hotel or club. Indoor venues pull casual toward its dressier end; dress as for a nice dinner.
• It is held in a house of worship. Emily Post suggests asking whether the couple's religion or culture requires head coverings, and whether bare shoulders, bare arms or open-toed shoes would cause offense. It also notes that some parts of the country are more conservative than others.
• The invitation says "dressy casual." That is a different code, one rung up, with a jacket on every men's version; the dressy casual guide has those lists.
• You can't tell. Check the wedding website, or ask the couple or someone in the wedding party. Then dress for the more tailored reading and bring a layer you can remove: a blazer for men, a cardigan or light jacket for women.

When deciding what to wear to a casual wedding, remember the asymmetry: overdressing by one step is rarely noticed; underdressing by one step usually is. A jacket or a wrap is the cheapest insurance against either, because it can come off once you see the room.

faqs.question: What is casual wedding attire?
faqs.answer: Casual wedding attire is the dressy end of everyday casual: a sundress, a skirt or dressy pants with a blouse for women, and khakis or slacks with a button-down or polo for men, sport coat optional. Goldberg describes it to Vogue as "a step down (or two) from cocktail attire," where heels and ties are not required. Athleisure, graphic tees, flip-flops and white are still out.

faqs.question: Can men wear shorts to a casual wedding?
faqs.answer: Only in narrow cases. Emily Post lists shorts on its casual list "depending on occasion and climate," and Vogue says tailored shorts could be appropriate at a summer wedding, but neither appears in Emily Post's informal wedding columns. Wear them only to a hot, daytime, plainly relaxed wedding, keep them tailored, and pair them with a collared shirt and loafers. Cargo and athletic shorts are out.

faqs.question: Are sneakers okay for a casual wedding?
faqs.answer: Clean, all-leather sneakers are, for women and men; Emily Post includes sneakers on its casual list and Goldberg tells Vogue to choose a pair that "looks clean and fresh rather than anything overly athletic." Running shoes, gym trainers and canvas pairs that look worn are not. For an evening or indoor reception, loafers are the safer choice.

faqs.question: Is casual the same as dressy casual?
faqs.answer: No. Dressy casual is one rung higher on Emily Post's ladder: a dress, skirt and dressy top, or dressy pants outfit for women, and a seasonal sport coat or blazer with slacks for men, tie optional. At casual, the jacket is optional by day. If the invitation says dressy casual, plan on the jacket.
